name: Bugling

name: Camping

name: Canoeing

detail.title: Swimmer test, not the Swimming badge
detail.text: Scouts must pass the Scouting America swimmer test before the subsequent Canoeing requirements. The Swimming merit badge is not a prerequisite. For your application, describe canoe instruction, strokes, tandem and solo skills, capsize recovery, rescues and risk management—not just boat ownership. GTA 7.0.1.1 identifies canoe-related training routes, including Aquatics Instructor, council-approved canoe training such as Paddlecraft Safety, and ACA canoe instructor training; council can consider comparable experience. Ask the council aquatics and advancement reviewers to assess your record. For sessions, arrange Safety Afloat supervision, swimmer classification, appropriate life jackets, a safe venue, rescue coverage and weather and emergency plans.

name: Chemistry
experience: Chemistry teaching, laboratory work or chemical engineering
planning: Use age-appropriate permitted experiments, protective equipment, ventilation and proper waste handling; obtain facility approval.

name: Chess

planning: Provide boards, accessible instruction and opportunities for each Scout to play, analyze and explain rather than only watch.

name: Citizenship in Society
experience: Prior council-approved counseling and appropriate facilitation experience
planning: Discontinued for new starts February 27, 2026. Consult council about eligible existing work and the official transition notice; do not recruit new starts.

name: Citizenship in the Community

planning: Arrange permitted visits and meaningful service, respect political differences and confirm the required approvals before projects.

name: Citizenship in the Nation

planning: Support individual research and civic discussion; separate civic learning from partisan campaigning.

name: Citizenship in the World

planning: Use reliable current sources, respectful discussion and safe approved contacts; do not require travel beyond the actual requirements.

name: Climbing

name: Coin Collecting

planning: Provide safe handling and research resources; avoid pressuring Scouts to buy expensive items or using appraisals as financial advice.

name: Collections

planning: Use accessible collections, lawful acquisition and careful handling; respect the badge’s exclusions and individual project requirements.

name: Communication

planning: Plan individual speaking, listening and organizing tasks; obtain permission for recordings and protect personal information.

name: Competitive Gaming

planning: Use age-appropriate games and accounts, supervised online interaction, healthy time limits and good sportsmanship.

name: Composite Materials

planning: Plan resin and solvent safety, dust controls, protective equipment and permitted age-appropriate tools.

name: Cooking
experience: Home or professional cooking, food safety instruction or outdoor meal leadership
planning: Plan separate home, camp and trail tasks; address allergens, food storage, budgets, stove safety and the rules on reusing meals or menus.

detail.title: Good cooking includes planning, nutrition and safe outdoor practice
detail.text: Describe experience teaching food handling, meal planning, nutrition, budgeting, home cooking and outdoor stove or fire methods. A professional chef title is evidence of experience, not automatic council approval. Plan allergy and cross-contamination controls and age-appropriate knife, heat and fuel supervision. The badge has distinct home, camp and trail components. Meals counted for Cooking cannot also count for rank or other badges, and the specified menu groups cannot simply be repeated. Review the current requirement text for meal counts, methods, group sizes, approval and evaluation. A single troop dinner will not demonstrate the whole badge.

name: Crime Prevention
experience: Public safety, community prevention work, law or civic education
planning: Use safe observation and approved interviews; never ask Scouts to investigate suspects or enter dangerous situations.

name: Cybersecurity
experience: Information security, IT administration, software security or cyber education
planning: Use authorized training systems only; protect credentials and youth data and prohibit unauthorized probing of real systems.

name: Cycling
experience: Bicycle instruction, maintenance, road riding leadership or trail coaching
planning: Check current route options, bicycle condition, helmets, traffic rules, health, distances and supervision; do not substitute unrequired distances.

name: Dentistry

planning: Use models and approved demonstrations; protect patient confidentiality and arrange consent for any clinical observation.

name: Digital Technology

planning: Check First Aid badge and other required components; use safe simulations rather than real hazardous incidents and coordinate with unit emergency plans.

detail.title: Care experience and CPR instructor authority are separate
detail.text: Describe current first aid education, practical experience and ability to teach safe, age-appropriate skills. Health care employment or a CPR provider card does not by itself establish CPR instructor qualification. The GTA requires CPR instruction to be given by a currently trained CPR instructor from a nationally certified provider. Arrange that instructor where required. Use approved training devices, safe role play, infection-control precautions and individual demonstrations. Badge completion does not itself award a professional first aid or CPR certification. Use current badge requirements rather than an old rank-prerequisite checklist.

detail.title: Knot knowledge must extend to safe projects
detail.text: Describe teaching knots, splices, lashings, rope care, anchors and safe project planning. Owning rope and spars is helpful but does not establish that a bridge or tower is safe for people. The current badge expressly refers to Guide to Safe Scouting height restrictions. Check those restrictions, permitted activities, tools, loading, material condition, fall and pinch hazards and supervision before choosing a project. Obtain the counselor approval the requirement calls for before the major project; do not improvise climbing or elevated structures under the label of pioneering.

name: Scuba Diving
experience: Recognized diver certification, dive experience and a plan to partner with a recognized scuba instructor
planning: Identify the exact certification level. A diver card is not an instructor credential; arrange agency-compliant medical screening, instruction, equipment and qualified supervision.

detail.title: A diver card and an instructor rating serve different roles
detail.text: A PADI Open Water Diver certification is useful evidence for a counselor application; it does not authorize you to teach or certify new divers. Council must approve your counselor role and badge. The Scuba Diving pamphlet says counselors need not themselves be diving instructors, but scuba instruction must be conducted by recognized-agency instructors in good standing and approved by the local council. Partner with an appropriately qualified instructor for the Open Water certification requirement. Swimming merit badge must be earned before requirements 3–6. Record your agency, exact rating, experience and instructor partner. Check current medical screening, agency age and course rules, equipment, emergency procedures and supervision. Scuba BSA is a separate introductory award, not the Scuba Diving merit badge.

name: Sculpture

planning: Plan the actual required sports and records, safe conditioning, protective equipment, weather and appropriate coaching.

name: Sustainability

planning: Use consent-based household studies and realistic projects; protect family utility and financial information and verify actual tracking periods.

name: Swimming

planning: Arrange council-accepted instructor qualifications, Safe Swim Defense, swimmer testing and appropriate rescue coverage; being a strong swimmer alone is insufficient.

name: Textile

planning: Plan safe equipment, fiber handling and required experiments; use only age-appropriate cutting and production tools.

planning: Use safe observation points and adult-approved study; do not place Scouts in traffic or require unauthorized driving.

planning: Arrange authorized visits, vehicle movement controls and professional interviews; youth do not operate commercial vehicles as an improvised badge task.

name: Veterinary Medicine

planning: Arrange consent-based interviews and safe observation; protect clinical records and keep youth from unauthorized treatment or hazardous animals.

planning: Verify current prerequisite badge and skill requirements, river classification, appropriate instructor qualifications, rescue capacity and conditions.

name: Wilderness Survival

planning: Plan supervised shelter work, safe fire and water methods, weather limits and emergency access; survival exercises are not permission to leave youth unsupervised.

detail.title: A survival exercise remains a supervised Scouting activity
detail.text: Describe experience teaching shelter, emergency priorities, signaling, fire safety, water treatment and exposure prevention. Plan the required shelter experience with suitable weather limits, site permission, youth-protection staffing, emergency access and a way to stop safely. The badge is not permission to abandon a Scout, withhold needed supplies or create a real emergency. Assess each Scout’s actual demonstrations and discussions. Use current fire restrictions and low-impact practices; do not add risky tests as conditions of completion.

name: Wildland Fire Management
experience: Wildland fire science, forestry, fire prevention or qualified fire education
planning: Use safe observation and approved educational settings; Scouts are not deployed into active fire suppression or prescribed burns as an improvised activity.

planning: Plan sharp-tool instruction, safe spacing, first aid and suitable wood and tools; apply current unit and national tool rules.

name: Woodwork

planning: Plan guards, dust control, eye protection and age-permitted tools; adult ownership of power tools does not authorize youth use.
